The page hero is a designed banner and was left alone.

THE MASTER IS SQUARE, AND THAT IS THE RULE HERE, NOT A CHOICE. In media-with-text the row height is max(text column, image natural height) and .media-with-text__media carries no aspect-ratio of its own, so a non-square master does not get cropped to fit the row — it STRETCHES the row and the block stops matching its five square siblings. That exact mistake was made and corrected on /pages/fine-lines-wrinkles the same afternoon (Malcolm: the block is taller than the other five), and the fix there was to go back to 1:1. It was very nearly repeated here: a 1792x2048 (0.875) master was built and published at 16:58, which put the intro row at 754px against siblings at 660 at 1440. Reverted to square within the same session.

WHAT THE SQUARE COSTS, AND HOW IT IS PAID. Measured, not assumed: the profile reaches x=2045 of 2048 — the nose tip is 2px from the right edge and there is no margin on that side at all. At 1024 this block's text column is 512px against a 452px image column, so the text wins and the box becomes 452x512 (0.883). A CENTRED cover-crop of a square master then keeps x120-1928 and cuts 118px straight through the nose. Rendered and confirmed; also checked at three candidate left-trims, which do not fix it either (still clipped by 78px at master 0.961, by 38px at 0.922).

So the crop DIRECTION is moved instead of the crop being avoided: object-position 100% 50% on this one image pins the right edge, so the 1024 crop takes all 240px off the LEFT — out-of-focus hair and ear — and the profile survives intact. At every other measured width the box is 1:1, no crop happens at all, and the rule is a no-op. This is the same lever the page's own hero already uses (banner_text_width sets object-position: 78% center on the image-with-text-overlay), and the same pattern as hero_image_position on page.brightening-glow.

SCOPED BY FILENAME, in a new template-local custom-html section. Not by section id — those render as shopify-section-template--<theme id>__<key> and go stale on every theme copy — and not by class, which would over-match all six blocks. img[src*='...'] is unique to this one image, and if the file is ever replaced the rule simply stops matching rather than mis-applying. The section lives on this template only, NOT in footer-group, which injects onto every page of the store and has caused two separate site-wide faults this week.

No long-edge cap or re-compression below q95: 2048x2048 is inside the 3000px ceiling and the theme's srcset tops out at 800w here. The CDN is what a visitor downloads — shopify-cdn-makes-source-compression-pointless.

NEW FILENAME, and deliberately not a prefix or extension of the 0.875 file uploaded at 16:58 — Shopify Files suffixes a name collision and keeps serving the original, and a stem that prefixes another has previously bound two slots to the same file while polling. The 0.875 file and the pro-collagen cream texture both stay in Files and simply stop being referenced.
